report_name: Revolut Data Breach Exposes Customer PII and ID Documents

threat_actors.name: Unnamed Social Engineering Actor
threat_actors.description: An unnamed threat actor who impersonated a government agency to conduct a 'sophisticated' social engineering attack against Revolut, resulting in a data breach affecting nearly 700 customers.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor conducted a targeted social engineering attack by impersonating a government agency to trick Revolut into handing over sensitive customer data. This is a form of business email compromise (BEC) or spear phishing targeting internal company procedures.

identities.name: Revolut
identities.description: A leading European financial technology company that was the victim of a social engineering attack, leading to a data breach.

identities.name: Revolut Customers
identities.description: Nearly 700 customers of Revolut whose personal identifiable information (PII), bank account numbers, and identity documents were exposed in the data breach.

indicators.name: Suspicious Email Header Mismatch
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Email Header Mismatch
id: 2b9a1c8d-4e6f-4b1a-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects emails where the From and Reply-To header domains do not match, which can be an indicator of email spoofing or impersonation attempts.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-20
references:
  - https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/20/week-in-review-cisco-patches-exploited-email-gateway-0-day-revolut-breach/
level: medium
logsource:
  category: email
detection:
  selection:
    header.from|re: '@(.+)'
    header.reply_to|re: '@(.+)'
  filter:
    header.from: '{{header.reply_to}}'
  condition: selection and not filter
tags:
  - attack.t1566
indicators.description: Detects emails with mismatched From and Reply-To fields, a common sign of email spoofing or impersonation as described in the hunting hints.

indicators.name: Lookalike Government Agency Domain Access
indicators.pattern:
title: Lookalike Government Agency Domain Access
id: 8d7c6b5a-4f3e-4d2c-8b1a-0e9f8d7c6b5a
status: experimental
description: Detects network traffic to or from typosquatted or lookalike domains mimicking legitimate government agencies. This rule is a template and requires customization with legitimate government domains relevant to the organization.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-20
references:
  - https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/20/week-in-review-cisco-patches-exploited-email-gateway-0-day-revolut-breach/
level: medium
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|contains:
      - 'fbi-gov.com' # Example lookalike
      - 'doj-us.org' # Example lookalike
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate but unofficial domains.
  - This is a template rule and will require tuning.
tags:
  - attack.t1566
indicators.description: Detects access to typosquatted or lookalike domains impersonating government agencies, a potential vector for the social engineering attack.

indicators.name: Unusual Bulk Customer Data Request
indicators.pattern:
title: Unusual Bulk Customer Data Request
id: 5a4b3c2d-1e9f-4a8b-9c7d-6e5f4d3c2b1a
status: experimental
description: Detects internal audit or application logs for requests involving bulk customer data exports, especially those deviating from standard procedure, which could indicate a social engineering attempt.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-20
references:
  - https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/20/week-in-review-cisco-patches-exploited-email-gateway-0-day-revolut-breach/
level: high
logsource:
  category: audit
detection:
  keywords:
    - 'bulk customer data'
    - 'PII export request'
    - 'government data request'
  condition: keywords
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate, authorized data requests.
  - Rule requires tuning to specific log formats and baselining of normal activity.
tags:
  - attack.t1566
indicators.description: Detects unusual internal requests for bulk customer data, flagging activity that deviates from standard procedures as a potential sign of impersonation.
